Executive Summary

This program is intended to meet the spirit and intent of the following regulations:
- California Accidental Release Prevention (CalARP) Program  Title 19 CCR, Division 5, Chapter 2
- Federal EPA Risk Management Program (RMP) - Title 40 CFR §68
- California Process Safety Management (PSM) Program, Title 8 CCR §5189
- Federal Process Safety Management (PSM) Program, Title 29 CFR §1910.119

Hereafter this program will be referred to as the RMP-PSM program.

This program is intended to be a "living document". As such, the information, procedures, policies, and documentation that make up this program must be made easily accessible and updated as necessary. To accomplish this, O'Neill Vintners & Distillers has elected to use PSMWriter, software developed and distributed by Resource Compliance, Inc. This software will assist us with updating, maintaining, scheduling, and tracking RMP-PSM related activities. 

1.1 O'Neill Vintners & Distillers, Risk and Process Safety Management Program

This is to inform all interested persons, including employees, that O'Neill Vintners & Distillers has developed their unified RMP-PSM Program. This program has been prepared to address the risks involved in operating and maintaining the following processes which have the presence of hazardous chemicals above threshold quantities: 

Process Name                | Process Chemical               | Process Quantity(lbs.)
P1 - Main Processing          Anhydrous Ammonia                27,000
P2 - 900 Farm                         Anhydrous Ammonia               15,000
P4 - Sulfur Dioxide              Sulfur Dioxide                               8,000
P5 - Remote 900                   Anhydrous Ammonia               12,500
P7 - Aqueous Ammonia     Aqueous Ammonia                   65,000

Note: Process 3 (Trailer Package) was decommissioned in 2016 with the installation of Process 5. Process 5 was designed by Axiom Engineers and installed by Cold Storage Technologies. 
 
Our RMP

-PSM program promotes overall plant, worker, and public safety. The program enables our facility to prevent the occurrence, and minimize the consequences, of significant releases of hazardous chemicals. 

Overall, the program is designed to prevent accidental fatalities, injuries, illnesses and physical property damage.

Our company has many policies and procedures in place to promote overall plant, worker and public safety. We have: 
1. Prepared a unified program based on the PSM plan to meet CalARP and RMP obligations as well
2. Organized the program so that it meshes closely with general business practices
3. Utilized PSMWriter software to ensure that all necessary employees have access to relevant information (SOPs, PHAs, audits, etc.)

The RMP-PSM program sets forth rules, procedures and practices that will help our employees and neighbors protect themselves.

1.2 Process Descriptions

1.2.1 Facility Overview

O'Neill Vintners & Distillers operates a processing facility for wine and other alcoholic beverages in Parlier, CA. 

Process 1, 2, and 5 - Anhydrous Ammonia

The facility has three ammonia refrigeration systems that provide refrigeration capacity to the following:

Process 1 - Main Processing
(9) Shell & Tube Heat Exchangers
(3) Plate Heat Exchangers

Process 2 - 900 Tank Farm
(2) Shell & Tube Heat Exchangers

Process 5 - Remote 900
(3) Shell & Tube Heat Exchangers
(1) Plate Heat Exchanger

Note: Process 3 (Trailer Package) was decommissioned in 2016 with the installation of Process 5. 

Process 4 - Sulfur Dioxide

O'Neill Vintners & Distillers has one (1) sulfur-dioxide process, which is used as a preservative to extend the life of wine produced. The sulfur-dioxide process consists of four (4) one-ton containers.

1.2.1.3 Process 7 - Aqueous Ammonia

The aqueous ammonia process at O'Neill Vintners & Distillers involves the storage and transfer of 30% aqueous ammonia to the EQ (equalizer) tank for the purpose of adjusting the pH of effluent water.

1.2.2

Facility Location

O'Neill Vintners & Distillers is located at 8418 S Lac Jac Ave., Parlier, CA 93648. The latitude and longitude of the high pressure receiver for Process 1 is 36.612299, -119.482976. The facility is located approximately 7.5 miles northeast of state highway 99 in a rural area surrounded primarily by agricultural land.

According to FEMA Flood Map Service, the facility is located in "an area of minimal flood hazard".

O'Neill Vintners & Distillers is not located in an Alquist-Priolo Fault Zone as defined by the California Department of Conservation. In addition, a review of United States Geological Survey (USGS) fault maps revealed that there are no faults in close proximity to the site. The USGS 2018 One-Year Model revealed that O'Neill Vintners & Distillers has a <1% chance of experiencing "potentially minor-damage" due to ground shaking in 2018.

1.2.3 Description of Covered Processes

1.2.3.1 Anhydrous Ammonia

The refrigerated areas are equipped with shell & tube or plate & frame heat exchangers and accumulators as required for flooded operation.

1.2.4 Process Classification

Each individual process at O'Neill Vintners & Distillers consists of vessels, equipment, and/or valves which are interconnected by piping. The processes are neither interconnected nor co-located relative to each other. As such, the systems at O'Neill Vintners & Distillers are treated as six (6) independent processes; three Anhydrous Ammonia refrigeration processes (P1, P2, and P5), one Sulfur Dioxide process (P4), and one Aqueous Ammonia process (P7).

1.3 General Accident Release & Chemical Specific Prevention Steps

1.3.1 General 

We inform our employees engaged in process operations of the dangers of an accidental release of each covered chemical in annual safety meetings. During these meetings we also discuss preventative measures, such as evacuation, in order to be prepared for a release.

O'Neill Vintners & Distillers has also conducted an off-site consequence ana

lysis of worst-case and alternative release scenarios for each process. These are for the purposes of informing the public in the event of an accidental release. The results of the analyses are reported in PSMWriter and hard copy binders. 

1.3.2 Anhydrous Ammonia

The ammonia refrigeration process at the O'Neill Vintners & Distillers facility is an integral part of the overall business and operates most of the year. The ammonia process contains a total charge of approximately 55,000 lbs. It is extremely important that this process is maintained and operated in a safe and efficient manner. Management is committed to making sure that employees are made aware of the potential danger of an ammonia leak.

Our refrigeration personnel monitor the ammonia refrigeration process and keep an active log book of all procedures and transactions that pertain to ammonia. In addition, the process is checked frequently by one of the outside refrigeration contractors that we use. These contractors also assist in performing the annual mechanical integrity inspection of our ammonia equipment. 

1.3.3 Sulfur-Dioxide

The sulfur-dioxide process at the O'Neill Vintners & Distillers facility is an integral part of overall business and lasts for approximately five months out of the year. The sulfur-dioxide process contains multiple cylinders with a maximum inventory of 8,000 lbs. It is extremely important that these areas and associated injection processes are maintained and operated in a safe and efficient manner. O'Neill Vintners & Distillers is committed to making sure that employees are made aware of the potential danger of exposure to sulfur-dioxide.

Our personnel also monitor the sulfur-dioxide fumigation process and keep an active log of all associated procedures and transactions. In addition, the process is checked frequently during the season by the outside contractor that supplies the SO2 cylinders. The contractor also assists in performing the annual mechanical integrity review

of our process equipment. 

1.3.4 Aqueous Ammonia

The aqueous ammonia process at the O'Neill Vintners & Distillers facility is an integral part of overall business and operates most of the year. The aqueous ammonia process contains a storage tank  with a maximum inventory of 65,000 lbs of 30% aqueous ammonia.  It is extremely important that this process is maintained and operated safely and efficiently. O'Neill Vintners & Distillers is committed to making sure that employees are made aware of the potential danger of exposure to aqueous ammonia.

Our personnel also monitor the aqueous ammonia process and keep an active log of all associated procedures and transactions. In addition, the process is checked frequently during the season by the outside contractor that supplies the aqueous ammonia. The contractor also assists in performing the annual mechanical integrity review of our process equipment. 

1.4 Five Year Accident History

O'Neill Vintners & Distillers has had no accidental release within the last five (5) years.

1.5 Emergency Action and Response Plan
O'Neill Vintners & Distillers' emergency action and response program has been developed to satisfy the following requirements:
- California "Emergency Action Plan" - Title 8 CCR §3220
- Federal "Emergency Action Plan" - Title 29 CFR §1910.38 

Strategically, O'Neill Vintners & Distillers has chosen to be a non-responding stationary source. Our employees will not respond to accidental releases of ammonia. In lieu of responding to accidental releases, O'Neill Vintners & Distillers is implementing the following protocols:
The facility is included in the community emergency response plan developed under Title 42 USC §11003.
Appropriate mechanisms are in place to notify emergency responders when there is a need for a response.
Annual emergency response coordination activities are performed (Section 1.5.1).
Annual notification exercises are performed (Section 1.5.2).

1.5.1 Emergency Response Coordination Activities

The purpose of emergency response coordination activities is to coordinate response needs with local emergency planning and response organizations. The intent is for local response organizations to be made aware of the regulated substances at O'Neill Vintners & Distillers, their quantities, the risks presented by the covered processes, and the resources and capabilities at our facility to respond to an accidental release of a regulated substance. The emergency response coordination activities will consist of the following:
Coordinations will be completed at least annually. Additional coordinations will be made to account for changes at our facility that may affect the community emergency response plan.
Coordinations will include O'Neill Vintners & Distillerss emergency response plan, updated emergency contact information, and any other information necessary for developing and implementing the local emergency response plan.

Coordination activities will be appropriately documented. The coordination records will include the names of individuals involved and their contact information (phone number, email address, and organizational affiliations), dates of coordination activities, and nature of coordination activities.

The disclosure of information classified or restricted by the Department of Defense or other Federal agencies or contractors of such agencies is controlled by applicable laws, regulations, or executive orders concerning the release of that classified or restricted information.

1.5.2 Emergency Response Notification Exercises

At least once per calendar year, O'Neill Vintners & Distillers will conduct an exercise of the facilitys emergency response notifications mechanism. The facility will record each notification exercise utilizing PSMWriter.

Alternatively, the facility may meet the notification requirements through other exercises conducted to meet other Federal, state or local requirements, provided that the necessary notification is performed. A

dditionally, if a notification is made in response to an accidental release, this would also satisfy the notification requirement.

1.6 Planned Changes to Improve Safety

O'Neill Vintners & Distillers has implemented many policies and procedures to promote overall plant, worker and public safety. Nevertheless, O'Neill Vintners & Distillers continually strives to improve in all areas, including safety.

By utilizing PSMWriter software, all necessary employees have access to every aspect of the RMP-PSM program. This has improved O'Neill Vintners & Distillers' ability to communicate hazardous situations to employees and contractors. In addition, PSMWriter tracks all RMP-PSM related events so that O'Neill Vintners & Distillers' management team can ensure that the RMP-PSM program is being implemented.

O'Neill Vintners & Distillers has implemented all aspects of the RMP-PSM program. When a RMP-PSM program requirement is completed (i.e. mechanical integrity inspection, process hazard analysis, compliance audit, etc.) any specific action items related to that event are entered into PSMWriter, assigned a responsible person, and given a due date. Once the action item has been completed, the resolution can be documented using PSMWriter as well. A list of current or past due action items can be accessed at any time by those with access to PSMWriter.

In addition to utilizing PSMWriter to create, schedule, track, and document events, O'Neill Vintners & Distillers has also entered into a contract with Resource Compliance to obtain help with RMP-PSM program implementation.

For the future, O'Neill Vintners & Distillers now thinks of the RMP-PSM program as a living document. It is an interactive framework that guides safe action for O'Neill Vintners & Distillers employees, but allows for feedback and continual improvement. Through the RMP-PSM program O'Neill Vintners & Distillers will continue to maintain overall plant worker and public safety.
